newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey optimistic on U.S. inflation outlook.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey optimistic on U.S. inflation outlook.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Friday expressed optimism that the U.S. can keep inflation low.
Asked by a reporter whether he was optimistic that the U.S. could maintain current low inflation, Lindsey responded that he was "very optimistic."
When asked the reason that he was upbeat, he replied, "Faith in my colleagues."

Speaking to reporters after a speech to the Atlantic Economic Conference, Lindsey said he did not see any sign that America's continuing budget difficulties were undermining the dollar's role as the world's key reserve currency.
But he noted that many market players have merely suspended their concern about the U.S. budget outlook until after the presidential election.
Lindsey said the government needed to take action soon to deal with its fiscal problems. "Action soon is certainly something that is necessary," he said.
